{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#cor-quadratic-form-symmetric}

#### Derivative of a quadratic form with a symmetric matrix

If, in addition, $\matr{S}$ is symmetric (and, as in @thm-quadratic-form, $p \times p$ and constant with respect to $\vcoef$), then

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef} (\qform{\matr{S}}{\vcoef})}_{p \times 1} = \underbrace{2 \matr{S} \vcoef}_{p \times 1}.
$$

:::

::: proof

If $\matr{S} = \tp{\matr{S}}$, then $\matr{S} + \tp{\matr{S}} = 2\matr{S}$, so @thm-quadratic-form gives $\deriv{\vcoef}(\qform{\matr{S}}{\vcoef}) = 2\matr{S}\vcoef$.

:::
